title: driver-sql (Postgres): after publishing a datetime field changed to date, a date written reads back one day early when the server time zone is ahead of UTC (the column stays timestamptz)
body:
domain:server#4 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgWRcTEB3toGxnWvuvX

Filing gate: ① product defect on a public door, measured by the dev of #32590 (PR #32848, report 6836981745, `out_of_scope_findings`). It predates that PR: base `ee230a25` answers the same. class: a · Suggested-grade: triage to decide · lane: `domain:server` (driver-sql, Postgres).

## What happens

- A live Postgres object has a `datetime` field (column `timestamptz`). The field is changed to `date` and the object is published.
- The column stays `timestamptz`.
- With the Postgres server at `+08:00` and the process in `America/New_York`, a date written as `2026-11-12` after the publish reads back as `2026-11-11`.
- SQLite and MySQL read the day correctly.

Measured on live Postgres 16. Same result on base `ee230a25` and on PR #32848's head.

## Expected

A `date` field reads back the day that was written, whatever the server and process time zones are. Either the publish narrows the column to `date` when that loses nothing, or the date read door on a `timestamptz` column converts in a fixed zone and never in the server's local one. Whoever reads the driver decides which.

## Business reason

Any app on Postgres that turns a datetime field into a date field (a due day, a birthday) shows every new value one day early to users east of UTC. Nothing reports an error.

Reader who acts: `domain:server`, `packages/drivers/driver-sql` (Postgres temporal read and the publish column changes from #32848).
